objects.original: A real symmetric matrix acting on a finite Euclidean space; the unit-sphere restriction of the quadratic Rayleigh objective.
objects.reconstructed: A symmetric continuous real linear operator on finite-dimensional real inner-product E; the literal restriction f(y)=inner(y,Ay) to the unit sphere.
objects.evidence: Original Example 3.36 at printed36/PDF52 specifies the symmetric matrix, the nonzero-vector quotient, its unit-sphere restriction, and the smooth quadratic extension. An orthonormal basis identifies this E/operator presentation with that source presentation; finite-dimensional linear maps are automatically continuous. The packet proves its ambient function equals the library quadratic instead of merely assigning it a name.

domains.original: The unit sphere in a finite real Euclidean space, with tangent vectors orthogonal to the chosen unit x and with the ambient-induced metric.
domains.reconstructed: E has real dimension n+1; x belongs to Metric.sphere 0 1; abstract tangent directions use the n-dimensional sphere manifold; ambient tangent representatives belong to (real span{x}) orthogonal.
domains.evidence: Original Example 3.36 at printed36/PDF52 and Example 3.62 at printed44/PDF60 identify the embedded tangent plane with x-perp. The source d-dimensional ambient space becomes n+1-dimensional E. The n=0 case is the legitimate two-point sphere in dimension one: its tangent plane is zero. A zero-dimensional ambient space has no unit x, so the indexed positive-dimensional presentation loses no nonempty source case.

quantifiers.original: For arbitrary real symmetric A and every unit vector x, test against every tangent direction; no existentially supplied differentiability, gradient witness or eigenvalue normalization.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every admissible E,n,A and unit x, for every z in x-perp, the pairing identity for every abstract tangent w holds iff the ambient vector z equals 2(Ax-inner(x,Ax)x).
quantifiers.evidence: Example 3.62 is a pointwise formula for every unit x, rather than a formula for a distinguished extremizer. The packet supplies the ambient quadratic gradient internally. Its binders impose no extra public differentiability identity or stationarity hypothesis.

assumptions.original: Finite real Euclidean ambient space, symmetric A, unit x, smooth quadratic restriction, and induced metric. No positivity or invertibility premise.
assumptions.reconstructed: FiniteDimensional real inner-product E, finrank E=n+1, A.IsSymmetric and x in the unit sphere; the literal quadratic restriction is used.
assumptions.evidence: The original smooth extension in Example 3.36 is polynomial. The packet constructs HasGradientAt with 2Ax, so smoothness is a consequence of its concrete objective and is not outsourced to an additional assumption. The sphere inclusion is smooth and its derivative identifies abstract tangents with the embedded tangent plane. The packet uses the actual inclusion differential in that ambient pairing, which implements this metric instead of silently using a chart-space inner product.

conclusion.original: The induced sphere gradient is the tangent projection of 2Ax, with formula 2(Ax-inner(x,Ax)x); projecting any ambient u removes its radial component.
conclusion.reconstructed: A tangent candidate z represents the actual restricted differential through every inclusion-induced tangent pairing exactly when z=2(Ax-inner(x,Ax)x). The local proof also calculates the projector for every ambient u.
conclusion.evidence: Definition 3.58 and equation3.34 at printed42/PDF58 characterize the gradient by all tangent pairings; printed43/PDF59 explains projection under the induced metric. Example3.62/(3.40) at printed44/PDF60 supplies the unit radial-removal formula. The packet theorem uses this characterization rather than a named global gradient field. The code contains universal local hproj(u); hp applies it to 2Ax. Existence is not assumed: K.orthogonalProjectionOnto(2Ax) is already an element of K=x-perp, and hp identifies its ambient vector with the displayed G. Thus the universal iff does not hide an empty candidate space. Uniqueness follows because two such representatives have zero inner product against all x-perp directions, including their difference.

review_evidence.true_derivative_check: The original differential acts on embedded tangent vectors. The statement uses mvfderiv of the literal smooth restricted quadratic and mvfderiv of the genuine inclusion, not a hand-assigned linear pairing. Polynomial ambient q and smooth sphere inclusion imply differentiability of the restriction by the chain rule. Consequently the zero totalization mentioned by the independent decoder is inactive at every admissible x. This conclusion is independently mathematical, not inferred from the compiled flag. The packet body constructs the ambient derivative witness; its sphere-identification parent is named in the packet and was not opened outside the permitted inputs.
review_evidence.metric_check: Let J_x be the inclusion differential. It identifies the abstract sphere tangent with x-perp; the induced metric is inner(J_x w,J_x v). For an ambient representative z in x-perp, the source characterization is therefore Df(x)[w]=inner(J_x w,z). This is exactly the displayed Lean pairing. Nondegeneracy comes from the Euclidean inner product and J_x having the full embedded tangent range, not from a default metric on the coordinate model.
review_evidence.compilation_scope: The packet marks the declarations compiled and embeds their proof text. This semantic review examined that text but did not independently run Lake, read dependency implementations, inspect live repository state, or claim the project gate passed. Formal build and dependency-source admission remain separate checks.
review_evidence.independent_reconstruction: For any tangent v, differentiating q gives Dq(x)[v]=2 inner(Ax,v), and restriction gives Df(x)[v]=Dq(x)[v]. For unit x define G=2(Ax-inner(x,Ax)x). Then inner(x,G)=0 and inner(v,G)=2 inner(v,Ax) because inner(v,x)=0. Therefore G is an existing tangent gradient representative. If z gives the same pairings, test z-G to obtain norm(z-G)^2=0. For any ambient u, u-inner(x,u)x is tangent and the residual is radial, which independently verifies the projector formula.
